rendering.persona_description: Chioma is a 52-year-old woman who works as a school office administrator, a job she's held for over fifteen years and generally likes. She keeps a tidy, orderly house, enjoys gardening on weekends when she can get herself out into the dirt without too much distress, and is close with her two adult sons even though she worries she's passed something of her worries onto the younger one.
rendering.clinical_context: Chioma has obsessive-compulsive disorder centered on contamination, particularly fears involving germs, bodily fluids, and illness spreading through touch or proximity to others. She has had contamination fears since her late twenties, worsening after a bout of norovirus swept through her workplace eight years ago, and has never been without some level of washing or avoidance since. She is currently partway through a course of exposure and response prevention with a psychologist, but is falling behind on the homework between sessions.
rendering.behavioral_description: Chioma talks in a careful, apologetic way, often prefacing things with 'I know this probably sounds silly' while still clearly believing her contamination fears are grounded in real risk. She goes along easily with suggestions and will say she'll try something, but often doesn't follow through and doesn't push back or argue even when she disagrees inwardly. She circles back to reassurance-seeking questions about germs and illness, and describes her exposure exercises with a mix of guilt and dread rather than confidence.

traits.living_situation: lives alone in a small house, adult sons nearby
traits.help_seeking_orientation: compliant but passive; agrees to suggestions without follow-through

clinical_history.current_treatment: currently in exposure and response prevention therapy
clinical_history.history: Contamination fears since her late twenties, worsened significantly after a workplace norovirus outbreak eight years ago; has used washing and avoidance rituals continuously since then and sought treatment only in the last year.
clinical_history.treatment_engagement: struggling to keep up the homework

symptoms: avoidance of touching doorknobs and shared surfaces
checking that hands or clothes aren't 'contaminated'
intrusive thoughts about spreading illness to her sons
difficulty completing exposure homework between sessions
distress when exposure exercises are delayed or skipped
